newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes see Dec/Jan WTI blowout to 50 cents.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes see Dec/Jan WTI blowout to 50 cents.

text.p: U.S. crudes were firm heading into the final stages of Friday dealings, featuring a "squeeze" in the December/January West Texas Intermediate roll as many large players got caught short when the spread gained.
Dec/Jan WTI started the session valued at a 15 cts advantage for the prompt month, but steadily widened to trade at plus 50 cts by the mid-afternoon, traders said.

"The main thing going on out there is the squeeze out to 50 cts in the Dec/Jan. Some players were speculating that the spread would come in, but got burned when the opposite happened," said a crude trader.
Dec WTI was valued around $24.70 a barrel, more than 70 cts higher than Thursday's close. That number figures in the 50 cts Dec/Jan roll against an outright Jan WTI of $24.20.
Traders said grade activity has seen sweet prices remain steady, but further erosion was noted in the sours.

U.S. government sales of Stretegic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) crude continued to be the scapegoat pushing West Texas Sour/Midland lower. Traders said the WTS was done as weak as a $2.50 discount to the WTI on Friday, 10-20 cts weaker.
Jan WTS/Midland was a full $1.00 firmer than the Dec WTS, sold at a $1.50 discount to the WTI/Cushing.
Dec Postings Plus at Cushing was last sold at $2.27, with the Jan P-Plus at $2.15-$2.16.
Dec Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was solid at an 80 cts premium to the WTI, with the Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at 45-55 cts over the marker.
